summary_en: This study tests secukinumab, an antibody that blocks IL-17A, in people with metastatic melanoma who had a past immune-related side effect from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and are restarting that therapy. Secukinumab 300 mg is given under the skin, first 1 to 7 days before checkpoint inhibitor treatment resumes, then weekly for the first 4 weeks and every 4 weeks after that. The main goal is to measure safety and feasibility; the study is Phase 1.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa secukinumab, un anticuerpo que bloquea la IL-17A, en personas con melanoma metastásico que tuvieron un efecto secundario relacionado con la inmunidad por una terapia con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario y que están reiniciando esa terapia. El secukinumab de 300 mg se aplica debajo de la piel, primero de 1 a 7 días antes de reanudar el tratamiento con inhibidores de puntos de control, luego cada semana durante las primeras 4 semanas y después cada 4 semanas. El objetivo principal es medir la seguridad y la factibilidad; el estudio es de Fase 1.
who_for: Advanced metastatic melanoma confirmed by tissue examination.
Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy with grade 2 or higher colitis, hepatitis, or skin rash that led to interruption, stop, or steroid use.
Planned by the treating physician to restart the same therapy or add a second checkpoint inhibitor.
Adequate blood counts, platelets, hemoglobin, and liver enzyme levels.
not_for: Symptomatic brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Past or current non-infectious pneumonitis that needed steroids.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic therapy in the past 12 months (checkpoint inhibitor side effects excepted).
